name: libvisual
why: Audio-to-visual plugin framework is a genuine transform between sound and image, though it is a library at heart.

brief.what_it_is: Libvisual is an audio visualization library, with a command-line tool, lv-tool, for running visualisations. The README itself is only a few lines and points to a GitHub wiki for more. The wiki describes a library that the tool uses to run visualisations, and the scout notes describe it as an audio-to-visual plugin framework. Audio goes in and rendered visuals come out. I did not confirm the plugin design in the README or wiki.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no stated purpose. The wiki says the project is maintained by volunteers and asks users and coders to get in touch, and it has a Hacking Guide for developers.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the mechanism. The wiki's news posts say the core is now written in C++ and that the API is being reworked for 0.5.0. Visualisations are run through lv-tool.

commands_seen.context: From a wiki news post dated 5 Jan 2013: the command-line tool for running visualisations, and the way to get its help text.

brief.install_notes: The README gives no end-user install steps. Build from source: the 0.4.x branch uses GNU Autotools, and the master branch (0.5.x and later) uses CMake, both with Ubuntu/Debian CI workflows as reference. The CI runs on Linux and on Windows via mingw-w64. The Homebrew executable is named lv-tool-0.4, which points to the 0.4 line. No hardware, accounts, or runtime configuration were mentioned.
brief.standout: It is an older audio visualiser that is both a library and a CLI tool, with a plugin-style design according to the scout notes. The README points to a separate 0.4.x maintenance branch alongside a 0.5.x development branch, which is an unusual split for a project this small.
brief.status: quiet. The wiki's newest news post is dated 14 Jan 2023 and says development has resumed after a long absence. The latest tagged release is 0.4.1 on 2022-12-06, and 0.4.2 and 0.5.0 are listed as TBD. I could not see commit dates, so I cannot confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: The README is very thin and has no usage examples. The wiki news is partly dated 2013, so parts of it may be out of date. The 0.4.x branch takes bugfixes only, and master is in active API churn, so the two branches differ. The build differs by branch: Autotools for 0.4.x, CMake for 0.5.x. No license was seen in what I read. The homepage was reachable, so this is not an outage.
quotes: Development has resumed after another long absence!
fetch_log: https://github.com/Libvisual/libvisual: worked; README returned, but it is thin and points to the wiki and build workflows
